description: Each invoice's cost ratio is the mean of its per-line product-cost ÷ total-cost ratios.

d.request: For each invoice, calculate the mean ratio of derived_product_cost to derived_total_cost across all its line items, then show the invoice number, that mean ratio, the count of line items, and that mean ratio divided by the average of all invoices' mean ratios, sorted by the relative figure in descending order, top 10 rows.
d.sql: WITH invoice_line_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, order_item_id, CASE WHEN derived_total_cost != 0 THEN derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost ELSE 0 END AS ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items), invoice_mean_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(ratio) AS mean_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM invoice_line_ratios GROUP BY invoice_number), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(mean_ratio) AS avg_mean_ratio FROM invoice_mean_ratios) SELECT imr.invoice_number, imr.mean_ratio, imr.line_item_count, imr.mean_ratio / oa.avg_mean_ratio AS relative_figure FROM invoice_mean_ratios imr CROSS JOIN overall_average oa ORDER BY relative_figure DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: For each invoice number in `Invoice_Line_Items`, give the invoice number, the invoice's cost ratio, its number of line items, and its relative ratio. To get the invoice's cost ratio, divide `derived_product_cost` by `derived_total_cost` on each of its lines and average those line ratios, ignoring missing ones. The relative ratio is the invoice's cost ratio divided by the average of all invoices' cost ratios (ignoring missing values). Return rows only when that overall average exists. Sort by the relative ratio from highest to lowest, with missing values last, show the top 10, and don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH line_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost != 0 THEN derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost ELSE NULL END AS line_cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items), invoice_stats AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(line_cost_ratio) AS invoice_cost_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM line_ratios GROUP BY invoice_number), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(invoice_cost_ratio) AS avg_cost_ratio FROM invoice_stats WHERE invoice_cost_ratio IS NOT NULL), with_relative_ratio AS (SELECT inv.invoice_number, inv.invoice_cost_ratio, inv.line_item_count, inv.invoice_cost_ratio / oa.avg_cost_ratio AS relative_ratio FROM invoice_stats inv CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa WHERE oa.avg_cost_ratio IS NOT NULL) SELECT invoice_number, invoice_cost_ratio, line_item_count, relative_ratio FROM with_relative_ratio ORDER BY CASE WHEN relative_ratio IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, relative_ratio DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each invoice in `Invoice_Line_Items`, show the invoice number, the invoice's ratio of product cost (`derived_product_cost`) to total cost (`derived_total_cost`), how many line items it has, and that ratio divided by the average ratio across all invoices. Ignore missing values throughout, and return rows only when that overall average exists. Sort by the relative figure from highest to lowest, with missing values last, show the top 10, and don't round anything. Each invoice's cost ratio is the mean of its per-line product-cost ÷ total-cost ratios.
c.sql: WITH line_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost != 0 AND derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL THEN derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost ELSE NULL END AS line_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items), invoice_ratios AS (SELECT invoice_number, AVG(line_ratio) AS invoice_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM line_ratios GROUP BY invoice_number), overall_average AS (SELECT AVG(invoice_ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM invoice_ratios) SELECT ir.invoice_number, ir.invoice_ratio, ir.line_item_count, ir.invoice_ratio / oa.avg_ratio AS relative_ratio FROM invoice_ratios ir CROSS JOIN overall_average oa WHERE oa.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ir.invoice_ratio / oa.avg_ratio IS NULL, ir.invoice_ratio / oa.avg_ratio DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For each invoice, calculate its cost ratio as the arithmetic mean of its per-line (derived_product_cost ÷ derived_total_cost) ratios, then show the invoice number, that mean ratio, the line item count, and that mean ratio divided by the average of all invoices' mean ratios, sorted descending by the normalized ratio with nulls last, limited to 10 rows, excluding rows where either the invoice's mean ratio or the overall average ratio cannot be computed.
b.sql:
WITH line_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    order_item_id,
    CASE 
      WHEN derived_total_cost IS NULL OR derived_total_cost = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost
    END AS line_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
),
invoice_means AS (
  SELECT 
    invoice_number,
    AVG(line_ratio) AS mean_ratio,
    COUNT(*) AS line_item_count
  FROM line_ratios
  GROUP BY invoice_number
),
overall_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(mean_ratio) AS avg_ratio
  FROM invoice_means
)
SELECT 
  im.invoice_number,
  im.mean_ratio,
  im.line_item_count,
  im.mean_ratio / oa.avg_ratio AS normalized_ratio
FROM invoice_means im
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
WHERE im.mean_ratio IS NOT NULL
  AND oa.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY normalized_ratio DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;
